Step four. Practice. Quick drills, with the answer, and the reason, straight away.

blues: Thousands of songs share the same twelve bars. Here is how the twelve bar blues works.
It uses just three chords. The one, the four, and the five of the key.
In the key of A, that means the A chord, the D chord, and the E chord.
Bars one to four stay on the one chord.
Bars five to eight. Two bars of the four chord, then back to the one.
Bars nine to twelve. The five, the four, then home to the one.
Now listen to all twelve bars.
One scale fits over all of it. The A minor pentatonic. That is why the blues is where most players learn to solo.
This is one of more than two hundred and fifty lessons in Fretkey. Coming soon.
